result:
The api died at 03:14:06 because the disk at `/var/lib/stockroom` filled up, and it never came back for the rest of the log (which ends at 05:29:57). The cause was the `report-export` job, which wrote about 20 GB of CSV files in the eight minutes before the crash.

One caveat: every line in `logs/service.log` is dated 2026-03-09, not last night. If the outage you mean was on 7 October, this is the wrong (or a stale) log file, so check that before acting on it.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 03:05:00 | `report-export` starts writing a 512 MB file to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` every 12 seconds |
| 03:09:03 | Disk warning: `/var/lib/stockroom` at 91% |
| 03:12:48 | Last export file written (40 files, about 20 GB in total) |
| 03:13:30 | Disk warning: 99% |
| 03:14:00 | `db: could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device` |
| 03:14:03 | `api: transaction aborted, shutting down worker pool` |
| 03:14:06 | `api: exiting (status 1)` |
| 03:16:00 onward | `proxy: upstream api refused connection` every two minutes, 67 times, through 05:28:00 |

- **What stayed up:** web and proxy kept returning 200s throughout; only the api was down. Its last successful request was at 03:13:51.
- **No recovery:** there are no api lines of any kind after the exit, even though `docker-compose.yml` sets `restart: unless-stopped` for it. The log doesn't say why, or whether the disk was ever cleared.
- **Unrelated noise:** the `cache: slow command` warnings (100–149 ms) run at the same rate from 02:00 to the end of the log, before and after the crash.
- **Not in this repo:** nothing here defines the `report-export` job, so I couldn't see why it wrote that much or whether it cleans up after itself.
